end.summary:
Practised showing 11–20 as one bundle of ten and loose ones.
Saanvi identified that 14 can be shown as 10 + 4 and that the bundle contains ten.
They connected 17 with seven loose ones but did not complete the explanation.
Teach-back was not completed; the lesson ended when Saanvi asked to stop.
end.parentNote: Asha practised the bundle-and-loose-ones method using examples such as 14 = one ten and four ones. Saanvi repeated that a bundle has ten and linked 17 with seven loose ones, but the full representation was not completed before the lesson ended. At home, make one group of 10 small objects and add 1–9 more, then say the matching number together.
